title: The Capitol and the Temple of Jupiter
aka: Temple of Jupiter Best and Greatest
lead: The hill in Rome whose temple of Jupiter Best and Greatest was the chief temple of the Roman state. It burned in December AD 69 in the fighting between Sabinus and the Vitellianists, and was rebuilt by Vespasian and again by Domitian.

sections.b: Wikipedia says tradition credits Tarquinius Priscus with vowing the temple and Tarquinius Superbus with finishing most of it; Livy dates its dedication to 509 BC and Dionysius of Halicarnassus to 507 BC. Jupiter occupied the middle room, with Juno on the left and Minerva on the right. Wikipedia says it burned in 83 BC (Sulla's rebuilding was finished in 69 BC), in AD 69 (Vespasian's dedicated in AD 75) and in AD 80 (Domitian's finished in AD 82).

Tacitus tells the siege and fire at 3:69-3:75 and sums up the temple's history at 3:72. Josephus says the soldiers "plundered the temple of its ornaments, and set it on fire" (War 4.649). After the Jewish war Vespasian had the Jews' temple tax paid to the Capitol (War 7.218). The Gauls took the burning as a sign that Rome's rule was ending, and the Druids called it a sign of heaven's anger (Tacitus 4:54).

claude.title: A pair of fires
claude.body: Claude's own theory, set out in full on the chapter page for Book 3. In short: the Capitol burned in December 69 and the Jerusalem temple burned the next year, but the two fires belonged to opposite sides of the civil war, Vitellius's German soldiers and Titus's eastern army.
